label: Diagram 2.1
caption: Diagram 2.1 | Relationship of ramp gradient to the going of a flight
description: This is a line chart, with the title "Diagram 2.1 Relationship of ramp gradient to the going of a flight" in a green bar at the bottom, and the text "See para 2.3" at the top left. The vertical axis is labelled "Maximum gradient of ramp" and is marked 1:12, 1:15 and 1:20. The horizontal axis is labelled "Going of ramp flight (m)" and is marked 0, 2, 5 and 10. A single line runs horizontally at 1:12 from 0 to 2, where a point is marked "(166mm rise)". From there the line rises in a straight diagonal to a point at 5, labelled "(333mm rise)" and aligned with 1:15, and then continues in a straight diagonal of a different slope to a point at 10, labelled "(500mm rise)" and aligned with 1:20. Dashed lines drop from the point at 2 to 2 on the horizontal axis, and from the points at 5 and 10 to their corresponding values on the horizontal axis; horizontal dashed lines also run from the points at 5 and 10 to 1:15 and 1:20 on the vertical axis. Below the chart, a NOTE reads: "For goings between 2m and 10m, it is acceptable to interpolate between the maximum gradients i.e. 1:14 for 4m going or 1:19 for 9m going".
